title: Banking records reveal characteristics of financial abuse
title_zh: 银行记录揭示财务虐待的特征
abstract: Abstract The experience of financial abuse, a form of domestic abuse involving control over money and finances, can be severe and long-lasting 1–3 , yet difficult to document 4 . Evidence on the everyday experiences of victim-survivors in the context of financial abuse is drawn primarily from small-scale, qualitative surveys 5,6 . Using anonymized banking data from a major UK retail bank, we compared the financial outcomes of a group of female victim-survivors of financial abuse ( n = 5,428; identified from customer disclosures to the bank) with a control group ( n = 15,602; consisting of individuals with no known disclosures). The control group matched the demographic and socioeconomic characteristics of the victim-survivor group 7 years before disclosure. A comprehensive set of 373 transactional and non-transactional financial outcomes were analysed over this period. Results indicate that, compared with controls, victim-survivors exhibited depleting savings and increasing debts, culminating in missed payments and declining credit scores. They also spent less on self-care, incurred higher transport and legal costs, increased cash withdrawals, changed addresses and passwords more frequently and were more likely to claim welfare benefits. Our results demonstrate how victim-survivors lose financial independence, experience economic instability and suffer financial distress.
abstract_zh: 摘要：财务虐待是一种涉及对金钱和财务控制的家庭暴力形式，可能造成严重且长期的影响1–3，但难以记录4。关于受害者在财务虐待背景下日常经历的证据主要来自小规模定性调查5,6。我们利用英国一家大型零售银行的匿名银行数据，比较了5,428名女性财务虐待受害者（从客户向银行披露中识别）与15,602名对照组（无已知披露）的财务结果。对照组在披露前7年与受害者组在人口统计和社会经济特征上匹配。我们在此期间分析了373项交易和非交易财务结果。结果显示，与对照组相比，受害者表现出储蓄枯竭、债务增加，最终导致错过付款和信用评分下降。他们在自我护理上的支出减少，交通和法律费用更高，现金取款增加，地址和密码更频繁更改，更可能申领福利。我们的研究展示了受害者如何失去财务独立，经历经济不稳定并遭受财务困扰。
